title: Koko Eating Bananas
description:
# Koko Eating Bananas

Koko has `n` banana piles. The `i`th pile contains `piles[i]` bananas, and the guards return after `h` hours.

Koko chooses an integer eating speed `k`, measured in bananas per hour. During each hour, she chooses one pile and eats up to `k` bananas from that pile. If the pile has fewer than `k` bananas left, she finishes that pile and does not eat from another pile during the same hour.

Return the minimum integer `k` such that Koko can finish all piles within `h` hours.

## Example 1

**Input:** piles = [3,6,7,11], h = 8

**Output:** 4

## Example 2

**Input:** piles = [30,11,23,4,20], h = 5

**Output:** 30

## Example 3

**Input:** piles = [30,11,23,4,20], h = 6

**Output:** 23

## Constraints

* `1 <= piles.length <= 10000`
* `piles.length <= h <= 1000000000`
* `1 <= piles[i] <= 1000000000`

tests.description: One hour per pile requires max pile speed
One extra hour lowers the required speed
Single large pile needs speed above one
Single pile finished in one hour
Time equals pile count, so max pile speed is required
Two huge piles with only one spare hour
Ceiling division can be exact across piles
One fewer hour changes the ceiling threshold
Slowest speed is feasible when there is enough time
Answer is not a pile size

solutions.name: Half-Open Answer Binary Search
solutions.description:
## Approach

Binary search the speed range `[1, maxPile]` with a half-open style loop. For each candidate speed, compute how many hours are needed using integer ceiling division.

## Key Insight

Feasibility is monotonic: if speed `k` finishes within `h` hours, then any speed larger than `k` also finishes. That makes the minimum feasible speed a lower-bound target.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log M), where M is the largest pile
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Closed-Interval Answer Binary Search
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use a closed interval `[left, right]` and keep an `answer` variable for the best feasible speed seen so far. When a speed works, record it and search the smaller half.

## Key Insight

Closed-interval answer search is useful when the loop removes `mid` from the remaining range. The stored `answer` preserves the best feasible candidate before `right` moves to `mid - 1`.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log M)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Average Lower Bound with Early Stop
solutions.description:
## Approach

Compute the total number of bananas and start the binary search from `ceil(total / h)` instead of `1`. During feasibility checks, stop as soon as the hour count exceeds `h`.

## Key Insight

No speed below the average required rate can finish on time. This mathematical lower bound shrinks the search range, and early stopping prevents unnecessary work on impossible candidates.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log M)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Recursive Answer Binary Search
solutions.description:
## Approach

Find the largest pile, then recursively binary search the speed range. Each recursive call tests the middle speed and keeps only the feasible or infeasible half that can still contain the minimum answer.

## Key Insight

The recursion is the same lower-bound search over answer space. The base case `left >= right` means the smallest feasible speed has been isolated.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log M)
- Space Complexity: O(log M)
